chapter: Family, marching bands and the tavern
title: Retirement, grieving and a trip to Mexico City
summary: He retires in 1964, cares for his ill wife until she dies, then travels to Chicago and Mexico City where he meets Marie Dickerson.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: eight months before I lost my third wife. After my retirement from the board of education in 1964, I stayed home to take care of my wife who was ill at the time. This is February, 1964, and that lasted until October '64, when she passed. After she passed, I took two or three trips to kind of get over my grieving. The first one I went to Chicago to visit my sister and then I came back. At that time it was near the holidays and I had a couple of gigs during the holidays. In the first part of January I wanted to go to Mexico City. I've never been to Mexico before--I mean deep Mexico. So I drove my car alone to Laredo, Texas; that's right on the line of Mexico. I parked my car in the garage, took the train to Mexico City and I was there for about two weeks. While I was there, I met an entertainer who was down there visiting,
Marie Dickerson. She just happened to be there and we had a nice little time reminiscing with each other.
I didn't stay long but she was still there, she had been down there for some time before I got there.
I understood she lived in Mexico for several years.
So I came back after about ten days I guess and on my way way to the border to get my car and drove to New Orleans. I had a lot of friends in New Orleans.
I know you couldn't resist playing down there.
